From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every point that matters. Taken together, the limitation terms, deemed disclosure and buyer-knowledge bar would leave Wattlebridge with almost no recourse for the specific risks the Seller has itself disclosed.

## 0. The [STANDARD] labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

**Ignore the note and reject it in writing.** It says [STANDARD] clauses "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that we have "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." Nothing in our playbook or instructions supports that:

- The 20% cap, 18-month claims period and the Bluefen and Riverlark positions are all items where our playbook requires a different outcome or principal approval. None of them has been agreed.
- Almost everything material is labelled [STANDARD]. Nothing is labelled [OPEN], not even Tax/IP, which our playbook treats as open.

I have reviewed every clause on its merits. When we send our mark-up, the covering note should expressly say that we do not accept the categorisation or the claim that anything has been agreed. That prevents any later argument about course of dealing or estoppel.

## 1. Limitation package

| Issue | Seller | Our playbook | Push back |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | **Reject.** 20% is our conditional fallback and needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. We have none. Counter at 25%, and do not signal that a fallback exists. |
| **Thresholds (cl 12.2)** | De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k; only the excess recoverable | AUD 5k / AUD 50k; seller liable from the first dollar | **Reject.** The de minimis is 5x ours and the basket is 5x ours (about 1% of price). It is also a deductible, not a tipping basket. Together these would exclude a large share of realistic claims. |
| **Claims period (cl 12.3/13)** | 18 months | 24 months | **Reject.** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which we do not have. 24 months gives a full audit cycle after Completion. |
| **"Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Hidden general override | Categories must stay separate | **Delete.** This is the hidden override our playbook warns about. It would extend the general cap, thresholds and time limits to title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants by default. Limitations should apply only to General Warranty Claims and expressly exclude every other category. |

## 2. Fundamental / Title warranties

The Seller wants capacity and title warranties under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity." **Reject.** Title is the reason for the deal. If title fails, our loss could be the full AUD 24m, but the Seller's position would cap recovery at AUD 4.8m after an AUD 250k deductible, and only for 18 months.

Require a separate regime for capacity and title:
- 100% cap;
- a claims period of at least six years;
- outside the de minimis, basket and any knowledge bar.

## 3. Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to "all Claims of any nature," with no fraud exception. **This is a red-line issue.** Insert an express carve-out so that fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct sit outside all caps, baskets, de minimis, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.

This is not negotiable, and no one on our side can waive it. Australian law may limit some of these exclusions in any event (for example, misleading conduct claims under the Australian Consumer Law). Even so, the drafting must be express.

## 4. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2)

The Seller discloses the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." **Reject this general disclosure and delete paras 1.1 and 1.2.** Only specific, fair disclosure should qualify the warranties: identified matters, described with enough detail for us to assess their nature and scope.

The words "without limiting any specific disclosure" in para 1.2 do not fix the problem. The general disclosure is still made.

Two further points:
- **Para 1.4 (non-admission):** acceptable in principle, provided it cannot be read to limit any specific indemnity, Condition or Completion deliverable.
- **Stale data room cut-off:** the cut-off is 22 September 2026 and today is 5 November 2026. Require an updated, specific Disclosure Letter at signing, with no automatic deemed disclosure of updates between signing and Completion. Material new matters should trigger our rights, not cure the warranties.

## 5. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

The clause bars any claim for a matter known to "the Buyer or its advisers," including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. **Delete it.** It is a blanket constructive-knowledge bar, which is worse than actual knowledge.

If any qualifier survives, it should be limited to the actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals. Separately, Seller knowledge qualifiers in the warranties need named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. No qualifier may ever excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**Why the combination matters:** read together with sections 1–4, the Disclosure Letter puts Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar on the record. Clause 8.3 would then bar warranty claims for exactly those known issues. That is why each of them has to be dealt with through a Condition, a Completion deliverable, a funds-flow line or a specific indemnity, and not left to the warranties. Sections 6–11 do this.

## 6. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)

The Seller offers reasonable endeavours and treats consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. This is insufficient on both counts:

- Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30% (DD-002). It is a material customer.
- Disclosure para 2 confirms there is no final written consent yet and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. A consent document alone may be conditional and ineffective.

**Require:**
- a Condition Precedent of an effective, unconditional consent (or one whose conditions are satisfied), plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met, both delivered before Completion;
- the Condition to be waivable by the Buyer only;
- a Buyer right to terminate if it is not satisfied by the end date.

## 7. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)

The Seller proposes a release "to be provided following Completion" for about AUD 3.2m outstanding. The facility has not been repaid and there is no discharge (Disclosure para 3; DD-003 clauses 8.1 and 9.2). On a debt-free basis, this is unacceptable.

**Require:**
- a current payout letter;
- repayment made directly to Riverlark out of Completion funds, deducted from the price paid to the Seller;
- executed, effective security releases delivered at Completion, including PPSR releases and any release over the shares.

A post-Completion release is only possible with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. We do not have that approval, so do not offer it.

## 8. DD-005 bonuses (funds flow)

AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses are left out of the funds flow, with the comment that they are "a matter for the Seller." Nothing says who actually pays them. If the Company pays after Completion, the Buyer bears the cost. This is the silent exclusion our playbook prohibits.

Disclosure para 5 also confirms that on-costs are unaddressed: payroll tax, superannuation, and PAYG withholding mechanics.

**Require** either:
- a specific funds-flow line, treated as Debt or a transaction cost and deducted from the price, covering AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs; or
- express Seller funding, backed by an indemnity outside the general limitations.

Also ask the Seller to confirm how the continued-employment conditions operate and whether any further amounts could arise after Completion.

## 9. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but that figure is not bank-verified either way, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.

The real risk is that the Company does not own IP it relies on. A payment-only indemnity does not cover that.

**Require:**
- an indemnity broadened to cover loss from any failure of the Company to own, or hold sufficient rights in, the SOW3 Project Materials, and any Ironquay claim;
- the indemnity to sit outside the general cap, thresholds and knowledge bar;
- the SOW3 cure preserved: verified payment of all SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a Completion deliverable.

Do not assume the AUD 180k figure is correct. Ask for bank evidence and Ironquay's own account statement.

## 10. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)

The Seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Nothing supports that conclusion. Disclosure para 6 says access, scope and any notification requirement have not been established for about 1,240 records.

We should not overstate it either. There is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure in either direction.

**Require** pre-Completion covenants to:
- preserve all logs and evidence;
- continue and complete the investigation, ideally with an independent forensic reviewer;
- give the Buyer regular written updates and access to findings;
- consult the Buyer before any notification decision, regulatory contact or contact with affected individuals.

Reserve our position on a specific indemnity until the facts are clearer. Delete the materiality characterisation.

## 11. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)

The Seller asserts these are "ordinary-course operating costs." Its own Disclosure (para 8) says the material does not state whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. It also asks that the three be read together.

Our playbook position is to assess them, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction either way. **Request:**
- the contracts, with terms, termination rights and timing relative to Completion;
- whether the three are related or linked to any Seller party;
- whether any amounts are prepaid or accrued.

Do not accept the Seller's characterisation. Decide on Debt, working-capital or warranty treatment once we have the facts.

## 12. Tax / IP

The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." **They are not settled.** They remain OPEN and must stay as separate categories, outside the general cap, basket and time limits, as section 1 explains.

Our playbook does not assume unlimited liability or any agreed outcome. State that expressly in the mark-up.

## 13. Title evidence

The Seller relies solely on the DD-012 share register. Its own Disclosure para 10 says this is just the source relied on and does not represent verification. Our playbook treats the register as an internal Seller document, not independent proof.

**Require:**
- a current ASIC company extract (as evidence, not as deemed disclosure);
- share certificates;
- the constitution, to check for transfer restrictions and pre-emption rights;
- PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company;
- Seller board resolutions and authority to sell;
- releases of any encumbrance over the shares, including any Riverlark share security;
- title and capacity warranties under the fundamental regime in section 2.

## 14. Lower-priority items to verify

- **Office lease (DD-007):** confirm the notification obligation, its timing, and that no landlord consent is needed. Add it as a Completion deliverable or covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** confirm with counsel that the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale, for example through a deemed-assignment or change-of-control clause.

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the [STANDARD] / "already agreed" framing** in writing. Review everything.
2. **Cap:** 25% / AUD 6m. No 20% without Amelia Frost's written authority.
3. **Thresholds:** AUD 5k de minimis; AUD 50k tipping basket, first dollar.
4. **Claims period:** 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" override.
5. **Title and capacity:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
6. **Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct:** full carve-out from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-waivable.
7. **Disclosure:** specific and fair only. Delete the data-room and public-register deemed disclosure. Require an updated letter, with no automatic cure.
8. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. Any qualifier uses named persons plus reasonable enquiry and never applies to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities.
9. **Bluefen:** a CP of effective consent plus evidence the conditions are satisfied, before Completion.
10. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases at Completion.
11. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line or Seller-funded.
12. **Ironquay:** a broadened IP indemnity, with the SOW3 cure (verified payment plus confirmatory assignment) preserved.
13. **DD-006:** preservation, investigation and update covenants. Make no assumptions either way.
14. **Sandbar:** request documents and assess. No automatic classification.
15. **Tax/IP:** remain OPEN, as separate regimes.
16. **Title:** independent evidence package.

**Escalation to Amelia Frost:** nothing in the Seller's draft justifies using either fallback (the 20% cap or the 18-month period). Neither may be used without her prior written authority identifying this draft. If the deal team wants to explore either fallback, raise it with her first. Do not put it to the Seller.
